headlines.text: Turning the clock back to 2024: Mercedes Mone vs. Kris Statlander went to battle over the AEW TBS Title, appearing on Worlds End, rated 8.58 ? an incredible outing. It was the 50th time the AEW TBS Title had been on the line, a genuinely rare milestone for that title. Mon? hooked Statlander's arms into a pinning predicament for the three count, retaining the TBS Championship in their second classic in as many months.

Rewind to 2022, when The Elite vs. Death Triangle settled things in a Falls Count Anywhere match on Dynamite, rated 8.94 ? a war that left everything in the ring in a wild trios sprint, on an outstanding New Year's Smash '22 - Night 1 show that earned an overall rating of 8.34. Kenny Omega put Rey Fenix through a table with a One Winged Angel in a Falls Count Anywhere brawl, tying the best-of-seven Trios Title series at 3-3 and setting up a winner-take-all finale.

Flash back to 2024, when Kazuchika Okada vs. Will Ospreay fought tooth and nail for the AEW Continental Title, appearing on Worlds End, rated 9.37 ? an instant classic. Okada hit the Rainmaker to defeat Ospreay and win the 2024 Continental Classic, with a returning Kenny Omega presenting him the title afterward.

secondaries.text: Looking back to 2024, when Will Ospreay vs. Kyle Fletcher met in a Continental Classic Semi-Final, setting the tone as the night's opener on Worlds End, rated 8.90 ? a match fans still talk about, on an outstanding Worlds End '24 show that earned an overall rating of 8.19.
On a Saturday in 2024, back when Konosuke Takeshita vs. Powerhouse Hobbs fought tooth and nail for the AEW International Title, appearing on Worlds End, rated 7.24 ? a solid showing.
Looking back to 2024, when Jon Moxley vs. Adam Page vs. Jay White vs. Orange Cassidy went to battle over the AEW World Heavyweight Title, appearing on Worlds End, rated 6.03.
